specDepthDecision.rationale: One plane and one PBR surface; preserve macro block layout, chamfer/joint normals and fine sandy face texture.

detailInventory.scanMethod: full swatch, PBR strip and two-way rotated grid

details.description: Interlocking zigzag block outlines run in predominantly vertical courses with local repaired irregularities.
Pale and medium grey faces alternate subtly, with a muted warm cement cast.
Fine pale sandy joints are bounded by darker recess lines.
Narrow worn chamfers soften upper block edges.
Fine mottled sand-cement grain covers faces.
Sparse dark oil-like spots appear especially left of centre and toward corners.
Several corners have small worn chips and imperfect junctions.
Subtle darker irregular patches cross some blocks without following all joints.
Fine hairline cracks cut across a few block faces near the centre and lower area.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: Explicit single 8 m quad at y=0, one root, no individual block geometry.
Retain grey interlocking block layout, fine cement grain, narrow joints and edge wear.
Independent PBR fields support dry matte concrete, restrained chamfer relief and local joint AO.
Inspect aligned 0/180 degree neighboring tiles; 90 degrees deliberately changes course direction.
Runtime/resource/export checks pass and whole-asset visual estimate exceeds 95.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
